component.name: HDR Finisher
component.summary: Finish HDR photographs and export gain-map images

description.p: HDR Finisher is an offline editor for grading HDR photographs, creating an SDR fallback, inspecting scopes, and exporting gain-map and HDR image formats.

On Linux, authoritative HDR presentation requires a native Wayland session, an HDR-enabled display, and an extended WebGPU surface. Editing, scopes, and exports remain available with a clearly marked SDR simulation when those requirements are not met.

Fixes problems found on 8 GB MacBooks, now the minimum supported machine: misread free memory, Full previews and graphics-card exports refused for lack of memory, and Grade controls blocked by the HSL picker.

Keeps HDR exports and Proof at or just below the Highlight Compression target, makes the Library faster and steadier on 8 GB machines, tidies panel borders and page tabs, and retires the Default Dark theme in favour of Modern Dark.
Moves export and Proof onto the graphics card with a CPU fallback, adds Retouch Heal and Clone, hue-selection masks and preset management, and speeds up Library browsing, rename, move and delete.
Fixes stale replies after switching photos, export queue cancellation, and several preview and Denoise ownership issues. Known limitations remain documented.
Adds the Photo Library and rebuilds Film Look with film stocks, print papers and lens filters.

Adds viewport-bounded GPU editing, adaptive Denoise, responsive Perspective drafts, and lane-specific Revert commands. Improves scope ownership, tiny-image previews, accepted-frame processing labels, and display capability changes.
Preview parity and timing limitations remain documented. Retired pre-1.0 adjustment fields are ignored; review older projects using wavelet Denoise or legacy SDR Match.
Fixes frontend pipeline synchronization and improves transformed path drawing, feather feedback, and four-handle luminance range controls.
Fixes native macOS window controls and adds local mask sub-masks, new themes, guided perspective correction, camera-linear RAW import, and smooth highlight compression.
Materializes HDR-to-SDR matching into editable controls and protects thin edges from Texture halos.
Adds Linux x86_64 support for native Wayland HDR presentation, Debian packaging, and Flatpak.
